h: Before You Kit Up, and What to Do After
p: If it's your first go at free-roam VR, a few pointers will help you get the most out of it. Wear comfy clothes and trainers, tie long hair back and leave any dangly jewellery at home. If you wear glasses, mention it when you arrive, as staff can help get the headset sitting comfortably. And listen carefully to the safety briefing, because knowing where the play boundaries are means you can relax and enjoy the game.

For parties and groups, it's worth deciding beforehand what sort of game suits your crew best. A mixed-age family group might prefer a puzzle adventure or a lighter shooter, while a gang of teenagers will probably be begging for the zombie horde. Getting the booking sorted early is especially important for weekends and school holidays, when parties tend to fill the slots.

Afterwards, you're in a cracking little town to explore. Macclesfield grew on the silk industry, and the Silk Museum and the restored Paradise Mill tell the story of the town's weaving heritage. The Treacle Market, a much-loved monthly market of local food, crafts and makers, takes over the town centre on one Sunday a month and is a great excuse for a wander if your visit lines up with one.

If you've got energy to spare, head up into the hills. Tegg's Nose Country Park, just east of town, has stunning views over Cheshire and the Peak District from its old quarry workings, and Macclesfield Forest beyond is perfect for walks. Further afield, Jodrell Bank, with its famous giant radio telescope, makes a brilliant science-themed day out for families.
